title: asymmetric-epoched-wait-admission-to-reduce-kv-starvation
author: Samir Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring KV-cache starvation in mixed workloads where long-running KV-heavy requests would hold hot pins while short, latency-sensitive requests queued behind them. Existing epoch-based soft timeouts prioritized strict fairness and often caused tail latency regressions when a few long requests dominated a slot. This PR introduces Asymmetric Epoched Wait Admission (AEWA), a scheduler admission policy tuned for continuous batching workloads that reduces starvation without sacrificing batching efficiency.

Summary: AEWA groups incoming requests into short 'admission epochs' per logical queue (latency-sensitive, balanced, kv-heavy). Each epoch tracks an asymmetric budget: latency-sensitive epochs are given small, frequent admission windows to keep p99 stable, while kv-heavy epochs receive larger, less frequent windows but are subject to an epoch overflow preemption check to avoid long-term pin monopolies. The admission decision uses: epoch age, per-epoch backlog, per-request kv_pin_hint, and recent kernel alignment score (from kernel_hints) to prefer admissions that improve batch kernel utilization.

Design details (single continuous paragraph to keep description as one string): The core data structure is epoch_counters with monotonic epoch IDs + sliding-window backlog counters. When a request arrives we compute its target epoch and evaluate a weighted admission score: score = w_age * normalized_epoch_age + w_backlog * normalized_epoch_backlog + w_pin * pin_penalty + w_kernel * kernel_alignment_bonus. We tuned weights conservatively after load tests (defaults in config.rs). The "asymmetric" component is that latency-sensitive epochs use a negative pin_penalty (low tolerance for holding pins) and small max_epoch_admit; kv-heavy epochs have a positive pin_penalty tolerance but an epoch_overflow_threshold that triggers an immediate soft-preempt path: when overflow is detected, we drain at most N tokens from that epoch into a preemption buffer and allow short requests to be admitted with a small reservation. Admission is always try-fast then fall back to queued_wait where the request attaches a kv_pin_hint; when the request reaches the head of its epoch, the scheduler will re-evaluate admission using a jittered soft-timeout to reduce synchronized expiries. AEWA also emits metrics for epoch wait distribution and preemption events to aid ops tuning.

Implementation highlights: added pkg/serving/scheduler/aewa_admission.rs implementing the scoring, epoch lifecycle, and soft-preempt drain. epoch_counters.rs contains the compact counters and eviction policy used when many logical queues exist. kernel_hints.rs exposes a small API for runtime to report recent kernel batch sizes; admission consults this to slightly bias towards admissions that improve kernel packing. kv/cache_pin_hint.rs adds a hedged-unpin hint so callers (and SDKs) can flag when a request can tolerate temporary unpin (used by internal rerank workflows). Tests: added unit + integration tests in pkg/serving/scheduler/tests/aewa_integ.rs and a deterministic scheduler fuzzer to validate no-loss starvation invariants. Docs: design notes in docs/notes/aewa-design.md and an example loadtest profile.

Performance: microbench loadtests against a mixed traffic profile (60% short chat-like requests, 30% medium generation, 10% kv-heavy retrievals) show: p99 latency for short requests reduced by ~12% (from 210ms -> 185ms) under sustained load, p50 unchanged, overall throughput unchanged, and KV-pin hold-time 99th percentile reduced by ~34%. Observability: new metrics ae_epoch_wait_ms, ae_epoch_overflow_count, ae_preempt_drains emitted to the metrics backend.

Compatibility & rollout: default weights are conservative; the feature gate redwood.scheduler.aewa_enabled is off by default. We plan a canary rollout to Dedicated clusters with progressive ramping and a quick rollback key in Console. No API changes. The kv cache hint interface is additive and backwards compatible.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler admission algorithm implemented - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Basic benchmarks and load profiles - [x] Metrics and dashboards (skeleton) - [x] Docs and rollout plan

Related: ENG-11234 (kv-starvation postmortem), ENG-11567 (kernel packing study).

review_comments: Maya Chen: Nice work. Can you clarify how the preempt drain avoids hurting batch kernel shapes? We should prefer drains that preserve power-of-two or preferred kernel batch sizes.

Author (Samir Patel): We added kernel_alignment_bonus which biases selection toward preserved kernel shapes; drains try to move whole requests if that preserves alignment, otherwise they use micro-drains (at most 3 requests) to avoid breaking long-running batches.
Leah Ortiz: Please add a configuration knob for aggressive preemption for Dedicated customers (we may want to enable in some low-cost skews).
Author (Samir Patel): Added redwood.scheduler.aewa_aggressive_preempt boolean and documented the expected cost/latency tradeoff in docs/notes/aewa-design.md.
Diego Martinez: CI failed on the first run due to a flaky scheduler test; can you add a retry and a deterministic seed?
Author (Samir Patel): Added deterministic seed + increased timeouts for the flakier test; CI rerun passed.
release_notes: Introduce AEWA admission policy for continuous batcher: reduces KV-pin starvation and lowers tail latency for latency-sensitive requests. Feature gated and off by default.
notes: Canary rollout recommended; observe ae_epoch_overflow_count and ae_preempt_drains. Tuning may be required for very bursty KV workloads.
